ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a smooth inclined plane with an angle $\theta=30^{\circ}$ (sufficiently long) is fixed on a horizontal surface. At the lower end of the inclined plane, there is a fixed baffle perpendicular to the inclined plane. A wooden board with mass $m=1\mathrm{kg}$ is placed on the inclined plane by hand. At the upper end of the wooden board, there is a small object (considered as a point mass) with the same mass $m$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the wooden board is $\mu=\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}$. Initially, the distance between the lower end of the wooden board and the baffle is $L=0.9\mathrm{m}$. The hand is then removed, and both the object and the wooden board are released from rest, sliding down the inclined plane together. The collision time between the wooden board and the baffle is extremely short, and after the collision, the speed of the wooden board remains the same, but its direction is reversed. The object just barely does not slide off the wooden board. The gravitational acceleration is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, and it is assumed that the maximum static friction equals the kinetic friction.

1. The speed of the block just before the first collision with the barrier is $v_{0}$.
2. The distance $x_{1}$ that the wooden board moves away from the barrier after the first collision with the barrier and when it is at rest relative to the block.
3. From the moment the hand is removed until the instant before the plank collides with the barrier for the second time, the magnitude of the displacement of the block relative to the plank is $x$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the inclined plane is fixed on the horizontal ground, and the inclined plane slopes downward to the right; near the lower right end there is a baffle perpendicular to the inclined plane; the wooden board is placed on the inclined plane, and there is a small object at the upper end of the wooden board; along the inclined plane, the distance L is marked between the lower end of the wooden board and the baffle, and the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal plane is marked as θ. Reasoning: Take the direction down along the inclined plane and pointing toward the baffle as the positive direction. Before the first collision, the object and the wooden board have no relative motion and slide down together from rest along the smooth inclined plane, with acceleration a=g sin30°=10×1/2=5 m/s². The distance from the lower end of the wooden board to the baffle is L=0.9 m, so before the first collision the common speed satisfies v0²=2aL=2×5×0.9=9, giving v0=3 m/s. At the instant of the first collision, the speed of the wooden board changes from +v0 to -v0, while the speed of the object is still +v0, so the initial relative speed after the collision is v_rel0=v物-v板=3-(-3)=6 m/s, with the direction being that the object slides downward relative to the wooden board. At this time the friction force on the object is upward along the inclined plane, and on the wooden board is downward along the inclined plane. Because μ=(2√3)/5, cos30°=√3/2, therefore μgcos30°=(2√3/5)×10×(√3/2)=6 m/s². Thus the acceleration of the object is a物=g sin30°-μgcos30°=5-6=-1 m/s²; the acceleration of the wooden board is a板=g sin30°+μgcos30°=5+6=11 m/s². The relative acceleration is a_rel=a物-a板=-1-11=-12 m/s². When the two are relatively at rest, the relative velocity becomes 0: 0=6-12t, giving t=0.5 s. During this time the displacement of the wooden board is s板=(-v0)t+(1/2)a板t²=-3×0.5+0.5×11×0.5²=-1.5+1.375=-0.125 m. The negative sign indicates that the wooden board is still above the baffle and in the direction away from the baffle, so at this time the distance from the wooden board to the baffle is x1=0.125 m. During the same time, the displacement of the object relative to the wooden board is x=v_rel0 t+(1/2)a_rel t²=6×0.5+0.5×(-12)×0.5²=3-1.5=1.5 m. Before the first collision there is no relative sliding; after relative rest, they can move together with g sin30° until before the second collision, and there is also no further relative sliding. Therefore, the total magnitude of the relative displacement from release to before the second collision is 1.5 m.
